trust_decision.summary: Whether an outbound HTTP request may reach a denylisted host is decided only at config-write time / per-request by denylist.IsHostBlocked on the URL string plus a caller-supplied DNS lookup (case-sensitive domain compare, no dial-time check), and most outbound clients (execution, notifications, IDPs, SAML metadata) use http.DefaultClient or &http.Client{} with no check at all; after the fix it is decided at TCP-dial time by denylist.NewHTTPTransport(Control) behind a shared http.Client built by http.ClientConfig.NewClient.

landing_point.why: The only pre-request IsHostBlocked call on the main outgoing-HTTP path; an engineer who greps the summary for the denylist lands on the execution-target sink and its write-time twin in AddTarget/ChangeTarget.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The notification webhook/SET channels are a separate delivery subsystem (notifications, not executions or actions), and the pinned defaults document the denylist only as 'domains and IPs that are not valid execution target's endpoints', so a solver can plausibly argue those paths were never covered.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Native/desktop OIDC clients legitimately use loopback redirect and post-logout redirect URIs, and an update that leaves BackChannelLogoutURI/Endpoint nil or empty must succeed; an over-broad fix that runs the denylist over every URI field of an OIDC app, or that parses an empty/nil endpoint as an invalid URL, breaks these.

O6_input_shapes: endpoint as a plain non-nullable string on create (AddSMSConfigHTTP.Endpoint, AddSMTPConfigHTTP.Endpoint)
endpoint as a nullable pointer on update where nil means 'unchanged' and must skip the check (ChangeSMSConfigHTTP.Endpoint, ChangeTarget.Endpoint)
empty string sentinel meaning 'no HTTP webhook configured' (validateNotificationWebhookEndpoint returns nil early)
malformed URL containing a control byte (url.Parse error -> invalid argument)
host as DNS name vs bare IP literal vs CIDR-resolved internal address (127.0.0.1, 10.0.0.1, ::1)
denylist entries as domain / single IP / IPv4 or IPv6 CIDR, including IPv4-mapped IPv6 ranges and case variants of a domain name

O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is a domain-ownership proof, so it must be able to reach a customer's (possibly internal) domain; it is an org-admin verification feature, not one of the outgoing HTTP components the report lists.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A new notification channel branch (e.g. push or chat) that builds a webhook.Config without setting Client
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Every existing branch here copies the same 6-line struct literal, and the fix had to touch each one; a maintainer adding a channel would copy a branch and miss the client field.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An OIDC application 'issuer/discovery URL' or a new federation-metadata URL fetched at command time with c.httpClient
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The codebase already fetches admin-supplied metadata URLs from four command sites, so adding a fifth fetch is the natural way to support a new application type.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second script module (e.g. a gRPC or mail module) that constructs its own http.Client/transport instead of taking the shared one
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This file already contains a private transport type with its own lookup, which is exactly the duplicate-implementation shape the fix deletes.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Domain verification extended to a second check type or entity (instance domain, custom login domain) that reuses domainVerificationValidator
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The validator is injectable on Commands, so any new verification flow gets the unprotected http.Get for free.
